structured.approach:
This attempt fixes the one G3 refusal. The claim that cited org.templates included the section numbers "2" and "7" ("sections 2 to 7"), and those numbers do not appear in org.templates.

What I changed:
- I removed the section numbers from that claim. It now names the template sections and says the TRD has a section for each.
- I made the same fix in the TRD's validation-check row that cites org.templates. It now names the TRD's sections instead of numbering them.

In this session I re-read every source the TRD cites:
- org/org.templates.md
- the three inputs: org.architecture, feat.prd, and the feat.prototype dataset section
- requirements/ZD-48600.md
- memory/MEMORY.md

I then rewrote feat.trd in full. Apart from that row, the content is the same as the previous attempt.

I checked every number in the claims against its cited sources:
- 3.9 and 22: org.architecture
- 30 and 10: feat.prd
- 75 and 1250.00: feat.prototype
- 2 dp, 02:00 and T2: requirements/ZD-48600.md
- decision and lesson IDs: memory

claims.text: The TRD template sections are components affected, interfaces/contracts, data, security and tenancy, testing approach and risks; feat.trd has a section for each of them.

The architecture is four repositories in one flow. ap_pipeline, ap_forecast and ap_aging run on Python 3.9. ap_portal runs on Node.js 22 CommonJS and renders HTML from JSON. JSON between services carries amounts as strings with two decimals and dates as ISO strings. Keep every existing signature; add new functions.
build_explanation_request(vendor, predicted_days, config=None) gains risk=None as its last parameter, so existing calls are unchanged. When risk is given, the prompt ends with ' Risk level: <risk>.'.
vendor_risk returns 'high' when predict_delay_days(history) > 30, 'medium' when it is > 10, and otherwise 'low'. It uses no LLM.
overdue_with_risk includes only unpaid invoices more than 30 days past due, counted in calendar days. An invoice exactly 30 days past due is excluded, and paid invoices are excluded.

The proposed JSON contract CT-1 has the fields id (string), vendor (string), days (integer, proposed), amount (two-decimal string) and risk (high/medium/low/unknown). Example row: SYN-INV-004, Synthetic Vendor A, 75, "1250.00", high.

renderOverdueRisk renders <table class="overdue-risk"> with one risk-<risk> row per item under the columns Invoice, Vendor, Days overdue and Amount, and returns an empty string when there are no rows. It outputs the amount string unchanged, without converting it to a binary float.

The Invoice data model is id (str), vendor (str), due_date (date), amount (Decimal, 2 dp), paid (bool), paid_date (date or None). Feed v3 adds an optional paid_date column. The schedule stays daily 02:00 Asia/Kolkata.
Lanes: ap_pipeline goes to Data Engineering, ap_forecast to Data Science, ap_aging to Backend and ap_portal to Frontend. End-to-end tests go to the Testing Agent.
Security scope: no finance posting, authentication, tenancy or payment execution. The tier is T2, and the risk label is advisory only.
The TRD applies decisions D-2026-031 (calendar days), D-2026-044 (Decimal, never float) and D-2026-050 (paid excluded), and lessons L-007 and L-011, with no conflict.

open_questions: TQ-1: Who produces the CT-1 JSON: ap_aging (proposed) or the end-to-end harness?
TQ-2: Confirm the interim handling of an unpaid row with a valid paid_date (map it, do not reject the row) until OQ-B6 is answered.
TQ-3: Does a vendor with no paid history get an entry in risk_by_vendor, and what does vendor_risk([]) return?
TQ-4: Confirm days as a JSON integer in CT-1.
TQ-5: Which rounding rule applies if an amount arrives with more than two decimals?
TQ-6: Should renderOverdueRisk render a non-conforming amount string as it is, or raise an error?
TQ-7: Which row class should be rendered for a risk value outside the four allowed values?
TQ-8: Where does the cross-runtime end-to-end test live, and which CI runs it?
TQ-9: Which date is as_of in production?
TQ-10: If bucket_for places exactly 30 days differently from the overdue rule, should that get its own ticket (with OQ-B5)?
TQ-11: If an existing portal helper formats amounts through a float, should that be raised against D-2026-044?
TQ-12: Should the owning lanes confirm checks V-1 to V-8 before the build and return any conflict to the Architect, or should a code-baseline review be added?
Carried unchanged: OQ-B1 to OQ-B10 and PQ-1 to PQ-6 (feat.prd), and PQ-P1 to PQ-P7 (feat.prototype).
structured.summary:
I rewrote feat.trd for FEAT-ZD-48600 in full and fixed the G3 refusal. The section numbers are gone from the org.templates claim and from the matching validation row.

The technical content is unchanged:
- 8 components affected
- interface requirements for all six functions
- the CT-1 JSON contract
- data, security and tenancy
- 13 tests, including the 30 and 10 boundaries
- 10 risks
- full traceability to the PRD and a decision-log check

The behaviour of the existing functions is covered by checks V-1 to V-8, owned by the coding lanes. There are no blocking questions.
